newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreigners told to stay out of Singapore politics.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners told to stay out of Singapore politics.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong has told Washington not to interfere in his country's domestic politics, state television reported on Thursday.
It said Goh was responding to U.S. criticism that his government was using a housing upgrade programme to woo voters ahead of Singapore's January 2 general election.
"They don't understand. They've offered their own health care plans to their own citizens. I'm completely all right," Goh was quoted as saying at a news conference late on Wednesday.
Government officials could not immediately confirm Goh's comments.
The United States criticised Goh and candidates of his ruling People's Action Party (PAP) on Tuesday over their use of the housing issue.

"We understand that ruling party candidates, including the prime minister, have warned that constituencies that elect opposition candidates will receive low priority in extensive government plans to upgrade public housing facilities," the State Department said.

"We believe that voters everywhere should be able to vote without fear of repercussions from government as a result of their responsibilities as citizens," a department press officer, Sharon Bowman, said in reply to a question.

Goh said on Sunday he would respect the voters' choice if they elected someone from the opposition, but added: "Then you'll be left behind; then in 20, 30 years' time, the whole of Singapore will be bustling away and your estate, through your own choice, will be left behind. They become slums. That's my message."
Goh's ruling People's Action Party (PAP), which has run Singapore since 1959, swept back to power on Monday before a single vote was cast.
Candidate nominations closed with opposition parties challenging only 36 of the 83 Parliament seats up for grabs, leaving the government a clear majority.
Upgrading is not the only programme the PAP has tied to victory for its candidates. Goh outlined at a Monday news conference a lengthy list of community development schemes.

"The point couldn't be simpler: the government will implement these programmes in wards where their candidates are returned; they won't be implemented where PAP candidates are voted out," a commentary in the Business Times newspaper said.
The opposition won just four seats in the last parliament, but that was its best showing since Singapore's independence.
